chunks: It is narrated from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام that a man came to him and said:
I have neighbors who have slave-girls who sing and play the lute, and sometimes I enter the privy and prolong my sitting there in order to listen to them.

He عليه السلام said to him, “Do not do that.” The man said, “By Allah, it is not something that I go to with my feet; rather, it is only hearing that I hear with my ears.” Al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام said, “By Allah, have you not heard Allah saying:
“Indeed, the hearing, the sight, and the heart — all of those will be questioned about.”

The man said, “It is as though I had never heard this verse from the Book of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, neither from an Arab nor a non-Arab. No doubt, I have abandoned it, and I seek Allah’s forgiveness, Exalted is He.” Then al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام said to him, “Rise and perform ghusl, and pray as much as appears fit to you, for you had been persisting in a grave matter. How evil your state would have been had you died upon that! Seek Allah’s forgiveness, and ask Him for tawbah from everything that He dislikes, for He dislikes nothing but what is vile; and leave the vile for its people, for every thing has its people.”

Then he mentioned the ghusl for al-istisqāʾ, and its mention has already passed in the hadith of ʿUthmān ibn ʿĪsā from Samāʿah. Then after it he mentioned the ghusl for the salat of al-istikharah and the ghusl for the salat of needs, and this indicates that.

key_terms.السَّمْعَ: hearing, as a faculty for which one is accountable
key_terms.الْعُودِ: the lute, a stringed musical instrument
key_terms.الْفُؤَادَ: the heart, the inner faculty of perception and intention

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام say about listening to singing and musical instruments?
ai.summary: This report recounts how Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام forbade deliberately listening to singing and musical performance, even if one does not physically go to the gathering. He cited the Qur’anic principle that hearing, sight, and the heart will all be questioned, leading the man to repent and seek forgiveness. The narration also connects repentance with ritual purification, prayer, and abandoning what Allah dislikes.
